title: Slow Magnetization Relaxation in Unprecedented MnIII4DyIII3 and MnIII4DyIII5 Clusters from the Use of N-Salicylidene-o-aminophenol

material_class.structural_family: Mn4Dy5 oxide-hydroxide Schiff-base cluster with fused Dy3 bowtie and Mn2Dy2 tetrahedra

synthesis.procedure: Reaction of Mn(NO3)2·4H2O, Dy(NO3)3·5H2O, saphH2, and NEt3 in a 1:2:2:2 molar ratio in MeCN gave a dark-brown suspension. Filtration afforded a dark-red filtrate and a brown microcrystalline solid. Slow evaporation of the filtrate at room temperature for 2 days gave dark-red prismatic crystals of 1 in 40% yield. Analytical data were reported for 1·2H2O; the crystal structure was determined as 1·10MeCN.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: one-pot reaction in MeCN; filtration; slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtration of the dark-brown suspension; slow evaporation of the dark-red filtrate at room temperature yielded dark-red prismatic crystals after 2 days

properties.summary: 1·2H2O shows dc χMT lower than the spin-only MnIII4DyIII5 value and decreasing on cooling, indicating dominant antiferromagnetic coupling and an appreciable ground-state spin. Frequency-dependent in-phase and out-of-phase ac signals in zero dc field indicate SMM slow magnetization relaxation.

synthesis.procedure: The same 1:2:2:2 reaction of Mn(NO3)2·4H2O, Dy(NO3)3·5H2O, saphH2, and NEt3 in MeCN produced a brown microcrystalline solid after filtration. The solid was dissolved in CH2Cl2 and layered with MeCN, giving after 3 days brown platelike crystals of 2 in 30% yield. Analytical data were reported solvent-free; the crystal structure was determined as 2·5MeCN.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: isolation of the insoluble brown solid from the MeCN reaction; dissolution in CH2Cl2 and layering with MeCN
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: brown microcrystalline solid from the MeCN reaction was dissolved in CH2Cl2 and layered with MeCN to give brown platelike crystals after 3 days

properties.summary: 2 has χMT slightly above the uncoupled MnIII4DyIII3 value at 300 K, rising then falling on cooling, consistent with competing ferro- and antiferromagnetic coupling and/or DyIII crystal-field effects and a large ground-state spin. Frequency-dependent ac χM′T and χM″ signals indicate SMM slow magnetization relaxation.
